DOC-001-v028::3.1::DEF-001.title: Definition: Self-Ballasted LED Lamp
DOC-001-v028::3.1::DEF-001.text:
Definition: Self-Ballasted LED Lamp
Standard: IS 16102 (Part 1) : 2012 (Clause 3.1, Page 6)

Self-Ballasted LED Lamp is defined as: Unit which cannot be dismantled without being permanently damaged, provided with a lamp cap and incorporating a LED light source and any additional elements necessary for stable operation of the light source.

Type is defined as: Lamps that, independent of the type of cap or base, have an identical photometric and electrical rating.

DOC-001-v028::3.8::DEF-008.text:

DOC-001-v028::3.11::DEF-011.text:

DOC-001-v028::1::SCOPE-001.title: SCOPE
DOC-001-v028::1::SCOPE-001.text:
Clause 1: SCOPE
Standard: IS 16102 (Part 1) : 2012 - Self-Ballasted LED Lamps for General Lighting Services - Part 1: Safety Requirements (Section 1 SCOPE, Pages [6, 11, 12])
Normative Force: MANDATORY

1 SCOPE
This standard (Part 1) specifies the safety and
interchangeability requirements, together with the test
methods and conditions, required to show compliance
of LED lamps with integrated means for stable
operation (self-ballasted LED lamps), intended for
domestic and similar general lighting purposes, having,
a)
a rated wattage up to 60 W;
b)
a rated voltage of d.c. supplies up to 250 V or
a.c. supplies up to 1 000 V at 50 Hz; and
c)
caps according to Table 1.
Recommendations for batch testing are given in Annex
C of IS 16103 (Part 1) : 2012 ‘LED modules for general
lighting: Part 1 Safety requirements’.
NOTES
1 Where in this standard the term “lamp(s)” is used, it is
understood to stand for “self-ballasted LED lamp(s)”, except
where it is obviously assigned to other types of lamps.
2 Higher wattage lamp is under consideration.
Annex A provides an overview of systems composed
of LED system and control gear.

Structured Requirements:
• rated_wattage: <= 60.0 W [Status: mandatory]

Standard: IS 16102 (Part 1) : 2012 - Self-Ballasted LED Lamps for General Lighting Services - Part 1: Safety Requirements (Section 4 GENERAL REQUIREMENT AND GENERAL, Pages [7])

4.2 Self-Ballasted LED
Lamps are non-repairable, factory-sealed units. They
shall normally not be opened for any tests. In the case
of doubt based on the inspection of the lamp and the
examination of the circuit diagram, and in agreement
with the manufacturer or responsible vendor, either the
output terminals shall be short-circuited or, in
agreement with the manufacturer, lamps specially
prepared so that a fault condition can be simulated shall
be submitted for testing (see 13).

DOC-001-v028::5.2::REQ-001.title: In addition, the following information shall be given
DOC-001-v028::5.2::REQ-001.text:

Standard: IS 16102 (Part 1) : 2012 - Self-Ballasted LED Lamps for General Lighting Services - Part 1: Safety Requirements (Section 5 MARKING, Pages [7])
Normative Force: MANDATORY

5.2 In addition, the following information shall be given
by the lamp manufacturer on the lamp or immediate lamp
wrapping or container or in installation instructions:
a)
Burning position, if restricted, shall be marked
with the appropriate symbol. Symbol
examples are shown in Annex B.
b)
Rated current (marked ‘A’ or ‘ampere’).
c)
For lamps with a weight significantly higher
than that of the lamps for which they are a
replacement, attention should be drawn to the
fact that the increased weight may reduce the
mechanical stability of certain luminaires and
lampholders and may impair contact making
and lamp retention.
d)
Special conditions or restrictions which shall
be observed for lamp operation, for example
operation in dimming circuits. Where lamps
are not suitable for dimming, the following
symbol in Fig. 1 may be used.
e)
For eye protection, see requirements of
IS 16108.
FIG. 1 DIMMING NOT ALLOWED

Clause 7: PROTECTION AGAINST ACCIDENTAL

Normative Force: MANDATORY

7 PROTECTION AGAINST ACCIDENTAL
CONTACT WITH LIVE PARTS
The lamps shall be so constructed that, without any
additional enclosure in the form of a luminaire, no
internal metal parts, basic insulated external metal parts
or live metal parts of the lamp cap or of the lamp itself
are accessible when the lamp is installed in a
lampholder according to the relevant lampholder data
sheet given in IS 9206.
Compliance is checked by means of the test finger
specified in Fig. 2, if necessary, with a force of 10 N.
Both joints shall permit movement in the same plane
and the same direction through an angle of 90° with a
0° to +10° tolerance.
Lamps with Edison screw caps shall be so designed that
they comply with the requirements for inaccessibility
of live parts for general lighting service (GLS) lamps.
Compliance is checked with the aid of a gauge in
accordance with the IS 9206.
Lamps with B22, B15, GU10 or GZ10 caps are subject
to the same requirements as normal incandescent lamps
with this cap.
Requirements for lamps with GX53 caps are under
consideration.
External metal parts other than current-carrying metal
parts of the cap shall not be or become live. For testing,
any movable conductive material shall be placed in
the most onerous position without using a tool.
Compliance is checked by means of the insulation
resistance and electric strength test (see 8).

Clause 8.1.1: Insulation Resistance
Standard: IS 16102 (Part 1) : 2012 - Self-Ballasted LED Lamps for General Lighting Services - Part 1: Safety Requirements (Section 8 INSULATION RESISTANCE AND ELECTRIC, Pages [9])
Normative Force: MANDATORY

8.1.1 Insulation Resistance
The lamp shall be conditioned for 48 h in a cabinet
containing air with a relative humidity between 91
percent and 95 percent. The temperature of the air is
maintained within 1°C of any convenient value
between 25°C and 35°C.
Insulation resistance shall be measured in the humidity
cabinet with a d.c. voltage of approximately 500 V,
1 min after application of the voltage.
The insulation resistance between live parts of the cap
and accessible parts of the lamp (accessible parts of
insulating material are covered with metal foil) shall
be not less than 4 MΩ. The requirements of IS 15885
(Part 1), Annex A, shall be complied with.
NOTE — The insulation resistance of bayonet caps between
shell and contacts is under consideration.

8.2 Electric Strength
Immediately after the insulation resistance test, the
same parts as specified above shall withstand a voltage
test for 1 min with an a.c. voltage as follows.
During the test, the supply contacts of the cap are short-
circuited. Accessible parts of insulating material of the
cap are covered with metal foil. Initially no more than
half the voltage prescribed in Table 10.2 of
IS 10322 (Part 1) for Class II luminaires is applied
between the contacts and the metal foil. It is then
gradually raised to the full value.
No flashover or breakdown shall occur during the test.
Measurements shall be carried out in the humidity
cabinet.
NOTE — The distance between the foil and the live parts is
under consideration.

11 RESISTANCE TO HEAT
The lamp shall be sufficiently resistant to heat. External
parts of insulating material providing protection against
electric shock, and parts of insulating material retaining
live parts in position shall be sufficiently resistant to
heat.
Compliance is checked by subjecting the parts to a ball-
pressure test by means of the apparatus shown in Fig. 5.
The test is made in a heating cabinet at a temperature
IS 16102 (Part 1) : 2012
of (25 ± 5)°C in excess of the operating temperature
of the relevant part according to 10, with a minimum
of 125°C for parts retaining live parts in position and
80°C (value 80°C under consideration) for other parts.
The surface of the part to be tested is placed in the
horizontal position and a steel ball of 5 mm diameter
pressed against this surface with a force of 20 N.
The test load and the supporting means are placed
within the heating cabinet for a sufficient time to ensure
that they have attained the stabilized testing
temperature before the test commences.
The part to be tested is placed in the heating cabinet,
for a period of 10 min, before the test load is applied.
The surface where the ball presses should not bend, if
necessary the surface shall be supported. For this
purpose if the test cannot be made on the complete
specimen, a suitable part may be cut from it.
The specimen shall be at least 2.5 mm thick, but if
such a thickness is not available on the specimen then
two or more pieces are placed together.
After 1 hour the ball is removed from the specimen,
which is then immersed for 10 s in cold water for
cooling down to approximately room temperature. The
diameter of the impression is measured, and shall not
exceed 2 mm.
In the event of curved surfaces the shorter axis is
measured, if the indent is elliptical.

Clause 12.1: Parts of insulating material retaining live parts in

12.1 Parts of insulating material retaining live parts in
position and external parts of insulating material
providing protection against electric shock are
subjected to the glow-wire test in accordance with
IS 11000 (Part 2/Sec 1), subject to the following details:
a)
The test specimen is a complete lamp. It may
be necessary to take away parts of the lamp
to perform the test, but care is taken to ensure
that the test conditions are not significantly
different from those occurring in normal use.
b)
The test specimen is mounted on the carriage
and pressed against the glow-wire tip with a
force of 1 N, preferably 15 mm, or more, from
the upper edge, into the centre of the surface
to be tested. The penetration of the glow-wire
into the specimen is mechanically limited to
7 mm.
If it is not possible to make the test on a specimen as
described above because the specimen is too small,
the above test is made on a separate specimen of the
same material, 30 mm square and with a thickness
equal to the smallest thickness of the specimen.
The temperature of the tip of the glow-wire is 650 °C.
After 30 s the specimen is withdrawn from contact with
the glow-wire tip.
The glow-wire temperature and heating current are
constant for 1 min prior to commencing the test. Care
is taken to ensure that heat radiation does not influence
the specimen during this period. The glow-wire tip
temperature is measured by means of a sheathed fine-
wire thermocouple constructed and calibrated as
described in IS 11000 (Part 2/Sec 1).
Any flame or glowing of the specimen shall extinguish

13.1 General

DOC-001-v028::13.2::GEN-001.title: Extreme Electrical Conditions (Dimmable
DOC-001-v028::13.2::GEN-001.text:
Clause 13.2: Extreme Electrical Conditions (Dimmable
Standard: IS 16102 (Part 1) : 2012 - Self-Ballasted LED Lamps for General Lighting Services - Part 1: Safety Requirements (Section 13 FAULT CONDITIONS, Pages [14])
Normative Force: MANDATORY

13.2 Extreme Electrical Conditions (Dimmable
Lamps)
If lamps are marked with a voltage range, rated voltage
is taken as the maximum and minimum of the voltage
range marked unless the manufacturer declares another
voltage as the most critical one. The lamp is switched
on at ambient temperature (definition given in IS 16001
and conditions as given in H-1 of IS 15885 (Part 1)
and adjusted to the most critical electrical conditions
as indicated by the manufacturer or the power is
increased until 150 percent of the rated power is
reached. The test is continued until the lamp is
thermally stabilized. A stable condition is reached, if
the lamp cap temperature does not change by more
than 1 K as specified in IS 8913. The lamp shall
withstand the extreme electrical conditions for at least
15 min, after stabilization is reached.
A lamp which fails safe and has withstood the extreme
electrical conditions for 15 min, has passed the test,
provided, the compliance (see 4.1 and 13.6) is fulfilled.
If the lamp contains an automatic protective device or
circuit which limits the power, it is subjected to a
15 min operation at this limit. If the device or circuit
effectively limits the power over this period, the lamp
has passed the test, provided, the compliance (see 4.1
and 13.4) is fulfilled.

13.6 Compliance
During the tests 13.2 to 13.5 the lamp shall not catch
fire, or produce flammable gases or smoke and live
parts shall not become accessible.
To check if gases liberated from component parts are
flammable or not, a test with a high-frequency spark
generator is made.
To check if accessible parts have become live, a test in
accordance with 7 is made.
After testing in 13.2 to 13.5, the lamp shall meet the
insulation resistance requirements of 8.1 except the
applied voltage shall be a d.c. voltage of approximately
1 000 V.

15.1 Method of Selection
The inspection test quantities (ITQ) shall be selected
in a mutually agreed manner such as to ensure proper
representation of the batch. The selection of lamps for
individual batches should be made as follows:
a)
Up to and Including 20 Containers per Batch
— Out of every container an equal number
of lamps (or as near to equal as possible) shall
be selected at random in order to obtain 25
lamps required.
b)
Over 20 Containers per Batch — Out of 20
containers, every distributed over the whole
batch, one lamp shall be selected at random
from each container to obtain the 25 lamps
required.
NOTE — Method of selection of lamps for type testing
are under consideration.

Standard: IS 16102 (Part 2) : 2017 (Section 3 TERMINOLOGY, Pages [4])

3.3 Lumen Maintenance (LED Lamp)
Ratio of the luminous flux emitted by an LED lamp at
a given time in its life to its initial luminous flux, the
lamp being operated under specified conditions.
NOTES
1 This ratio x is generally expressed in per cent.
2 The lumen maintenance of an LED lamp is the effect of
decrease of the lumen output of the LED(s) or a combination
of this with failure(s) of LED(s) if the lamp contains more than
one LED.
3 The lumen maintenance is also termed as luminous flux
maintenance.

3.8 Failure Fraction at Rated Life (Fy)

type, that at their rated life designates the percentage

components of an LED lamp including mechanical components,
as far as the light output is concerned. The effect of the LED
could either be less light than claimed or no light at all.
2 For self-ballasted LED lamps normally a failure fraction of
10 percent or/and 50 percent are being applied, indicated as
F10 or/and F50.

Clause 7.1: General Test Conditions
Standard: IS 16102 (Part 2) : 2017 (Section 7 TEST CONDITIONS, Pages [6])
Normative Force: MANDATORY

7.1 General Test Conditions
Testing duration is 25 percent of rated life time up to a
maximum of 6 000 h.
Additional LED lamps within the same family (see 3.13)
may be subjected to decreased testing duration. For
identification of a family, see Table 2, for details on
sample sizes for family testing, see Table 11.
Test conditions for testing tLED, electrical and
photometric characteristics, lumen maintenance and life
are given in Annex A.
All tests are conducted on n LED lamps of the same
type. The number n shall be a minimum of products as
given in Table 10. LED lamps used in the endurance
tests shall not be used in other tests.
LED lamps with dimming control shall be adjusted to
maximum light output for all tests.
LED lamps with adjustable colour point shall be
adjusted/set to one fixed value as indicated by the
manufacturer or responsible vendor.

DOC-002-v001::7.2.2::REQ-001.title: Variations within a Family

Clause 7.2.2: Variations within a Family
Standard: IS 16102 (Part 2) : 2017 (Section 7 TEST CONDITIONS, Pages [7])
Normative Force: RECOMMENDED

7.2.2 Variations within a Family
Each family of LED lamps requires a case-by-case
consideration. The range of LED lamps should be
manufactured by the same manufacturer, under the same
quality assurance system. The type variations of the
range [for example Correlated Colour Temperature
(CCT) given in 10.1] should be essentially identical
with respect to materials used, components and
construction applied.
Requirements for the identification of a family of LED
lamps for type testing are given in 3.13 and in Table 2.
The testing time may be reduced within a family down
to 1 000 h in case variations of part characteristics are
within the conditions given in Table 2.

within a family at initial and after reduced testing time
shall be in line with the values provided by the
manufacturer or responsible vendor of the lamp:
a)
Chromaticity co-ordinates,
b)
Colour rendering index,
c)
Lumen maintenance code, and
d)
Results of accelerated operational life test.
For all of the tested units in a sample, the measured
values of an LED lamp (the initial and maintained
value) shall not vary beyond the values indicated by
the manufacturer or responsible vendor.
The measured values shall be of the same category or
code as per the declared values or better. The maximum
number of LED lamps in a sample which can fail in
individual tests and in the groups is given in Table 11.

Clause 11.1: General

Normative Force: MANDATORY

11.1 General
Life of an LED lamp as defined in 3.6 is the combined
effect of gradual light output degradation, mostly caused
by material degradation (see 11.2) and abrupt light output
degradation, mostly caused by electrical component
failure (see 11.3). Endurance test is therefore carried out
to assess the reliability and life of the lamp.
The fraction of tested lamps of a sample (Fy) that may
fail to comply with the requirements of the tests
under 11.2 are defined in 3.3 and 3.8.
On request, reduction of luminous flux due to zero
lumen output and due to degradation of the LED
material in the measured sample may be given
separately.
NOTE — Compliance of lumen maintenance after 25 percent
of life time or 6 000 h implies that the lamps would have a life
of 25 000 h or as declared by the manufacturer with a failure
fraction of B50.

DOC-002-v001::ANNEX A::ANNEX-001.text:
ANNEX A - ANNEX A (Pages [15, 16, 17]):
ANNEX A
(Clauses 3.2, 4, 7.1, 8.1, 9.1, 9.2.4 and 9.2.5)
METHOD OF MEASURING LAMP CHARACTERISTICS
A-1 GENERAL
Unless otherwise specified, all measurements shall be
made in a draught-free room at a temperature of 27°C
with a tolerance of ± 1°C, a relative humidity of
65 percent maximum and steady state operation of the
LED lamp.
For air movement requirements, see IS 16106.
If not exempted by specific clause, lamps shall be
operated free burning in a vertical position, cap-up,
unless otherwise specified by the manufacturer or
responsible vendor.
a)
Operate the lamp and record the luminous flux
or luminous intensity and the lamp power as
temperature/time depending variables.
b)
During the stabilization, measurements of
luminous flux or luminous intensity and electrical
lamp power are made at least at an interval of
1 min. The LED lamp shall be operated for at
least 30 min and it is considered stable and
suitable for test purpose, if the relative difference
of maximum and minimum readings of light
output and electrical power observed over the
last 15 min is less than 0.5 percent of the
minimum reading. If the LED lamp is pre-
burned, it does not need to be operated for 30
min, and it is considered stable if the readings
of the last 15 min meet above requirement.
If the LED lamp exhibit large fluctuations and
stabilization conditions are not achieved
within 45 min of operation due to the
fluctuations, the measurement may be started
and the observed fluctuations shall be
reported. However if, instead of random
fluctuations, a slow decrease of gradient in
the measured values is still observed, then the
measurements should be started only when the
stabilization criteria are met.
NOTE — Normally the observed stabilization process
is a slow decrease in light output until thermal stability
is reached. However, due to the electronics, fluctuations
can still occur near thermal stability.
c)
The stabilization is strongly related to thermal
equilibrium of the components. A pre-burning
(operation of the light source prior to mounting
in the measurement system) may be applied
to reduce the stabilization time in the
IS 16102 (Part 2) : 2017
measurement system. In particular for
measurement of a number of products of the
same type, measurement time may be reduced
if it has been demonstrated that the pre-
burning method produces the same stabilized
condition as when using the normal procedure.
d)
The subsequent lamps are submitted to
stabilization (operation of the light source prior
to mounting into the photometer) on basis of the
stabilization time observed in step (c). Lamps
may then be measured after 15 min in the
photometer, applying the criterion of step (b).
NOTE — Normally the observed stabilization process is a slow
decrease in luminous flux or luminous intensity until thermal
stability. However due to the electronics, fluctuations can still
occur near thermal stability and stabilisation criteria not met.
A-2 TEST VOLTAGE
A-2.1 General
The test voltage shall be stable within ±0.5 percent,
during stabilization periods, this tolerance being
± 0.2 percent at the moment of measurements. For
ageing and luminous flux maintenance testing the
tolerance is 2 percent. The total harmonic content of
the supply voltage shall not exceed 3 percent. The
harmonic content is defined as the r.m.s. summation of
the individual harmonic components using the
fundamental as 100 percent.
The test voltage shall be as specified in A-2.2.
NOTE — The harmonic content is defined as the r.m.s.
summation of the individual harmonic components using the
fundamental as 100 percent.
A-2.2 Relation of Rated Voltage to Test Voltage
The test voltage shall be the rated voltage or the mid-
point of the voltage range as specified in Table 13.

A-3.2  Ageing
LED lamps normally do not require any ageing prior
to testing. However, the manufacturer may specify an
ageing period.
A-3.3  Luminous Flux
The initial and maintained luminous flux shall be
measured after stabilisation of the LED lamp.
A-3.4 Luminous Intensity Distribution
Luminous intensity distribution data shall be made
available by the manufactures for all variations of the
LED lamp and any optical attachments or accessories
that the LED lamp has been specified for use with and
shall be tested in accordance with IS/IEC TR61341.
IS 16102 (Part 2) : 2017
A-3.5 Peak Intensity
The peak intensity shall be measured in accordance
with IS/IEC TR61341.
A-3.6 Beam Angle
The beam angle shall be measured in accordance with
IS/IEC TR61341.
The beam angle is not determined by the half peak, but
by the half centre beam intensity.
A-3.7 Colour Rendering
Measurement of colour rendering index shall be made
in accordance with IS 16106.
A-3.8  Chromaticity Co-ordinate Values
Chromaticity co-ordinates shall be in accordance with
the values given in Annex B of IS 2418 (Part 2).
If the chromaticity is only related to a given direction,
the radiation angle shall be declared by the
manufacturer.
If the radiation angle is not mentioned, the chromaticity
is considered as the spatial chromaticity 4π (2π for
reflector lamps).
The manufacturer shall provide information on the
method used.

DOC-007-v001::3.1::DEF-001.title: Definition: Electronic Controlgear for LED Modules
DOC-007-v001::3.1::DEF-001.text:
Definition: Electronic Controlgear for LED Modules
Standard: IS 15885 (Part 2/Sec 13) : 2012 (Clause 3.1, Page 6)

Electronic Controlgear for LED Modules is defined as: Unit inserted between the supply and one or more LED modules which serves to supply the LED module(s) with its (their) rated voltage or rated current. The unit may consist of one or more separate components and may include means for dimming, correcting the power factor and suppressing radio interference.

DOC-007-v001::1::SCOPE-001.title: SCOPE
DOC-007-v001::1::SCOPE-001.text:
Clause 1: SCOPE
Standard: IS 15885 (Part 2/Sec 13) : 2012 (Section 1 SCOPE, Pages [6])
Normative Force: MANDATORY

1 SCOPE
This standard (Part 2/Sec 13) specifies particular safety
requirements for electronic control gear for use on d.c.
supplies up to and including 1 000 V and a.c. supplies
up to and including 1 000 V at 50 Hz and at an output
frequency which can deviate from the supply
frequency, associated with LED modules.
Control gear for LED modules specified in this
standard are designed to provide constant voltage or
current at SELV or higher voltages. Deviations from
the pure voltage and current types do not exclude the
gear from this standard.
The Annexes A, B, C, D, E, F, G, H and L of IS 15885
(Part 1) : 2011 ‘Safety of lamp controlgear: Part 1
General requirements’ which are applicable according
to this Part and Section and using the word ‘lamp’ are
understood to also comprise LED modules.
Particular requirements for SELV control gears are
given in Annex I.
Performance requirements shall be covered by a
separate standard (see IS 16104 : 2012 ‘d.c. or a.c.
supplied electronic controgear for LED Modules —
Performance requirements’).
Plug-in control gear, being part of the luminaire, are
covered as for built-in control gear by the additional
requirements of the luminaire standard.

DOC-022-v001::6.2::REQ-001.text:
Clause 6.2: Breaking Strength
Standard: IS 15622 : 2017 - Pressed Ceramic Tiles - Specification (First Revision) (Section 6.2 Breaking Strength, Pages [4, 5])
Normative Force: MANDATORY

Breaking Strength: Minimum breaking strength shall be 1300 N for tiles thickness >= 7.5 mm.

DOC-022-v001::7.1::REQ-001.title: Deep Abrasion Resistance
DOC-022-v001::7.1::REQ-001.text:
Clause 7.1: Deep Abrasion Resistance
Standard: IS 15622 : 2017 - Pressed Ceramic Tiles - Specification (First Revision) (Section 7.1 Deep Abrasion Resistance, Pages [5, 6])
Normative Force: PROHIBITED

Deep Abrasion Resistance: Maximum volume loss for unglazed tiles shall not exceed 175 mm³.

DOC-023-v001::1::SCOPE-001.title: Scope
DOC-023-v001::1::SCOPE-001.text:
Clause 1: Scope
Standard: IS 14543 : 2024 - Packaged Drinking Water (Other Than Packaged Natural Mineral Water) - Specification (Third Revision) (Section 1 Scope, Pages [1])
Normative Force: INFORMATIVE

Scope: This Indian Standard (IS 14543 : 2024) covers and specifies requirements for Packaged Drinking Water (Other Than Packaged Natural Mineral Water) - Specification (Third Revision). It applies to packaged_drinking_water under drinking_water category in the food_agriculture domain.

DOC-023-v001::4.1::REQ-001.title: Organoleptic and Physical Parameters
DOC-023-v001::4.1::REQ-001.text:
Clause 4.1: Organoleptic and Physical Parameters
Standard: IS 14543 : 2024 - Packaged Drinking Water (Other Than Packaged Natural Mineral Water) - Specification (Third Revision) (Section 4.1 Organoleptic and Physical Parameters, Pages [2, 3])
Normative Force: MANDATORY

Organoleptic and Physical Parameters: pH shall be in the range 6.5 to 8.5.

DOC-023-v001::4.2::REQ-001.title: Total Dissolved Solids (TDS)
DOC-023-v001::4.2::REQ-001.text:
Clause 4.2: Total Dissolved Solids (TDS)
Standard: IS 14543 : 2024 - Packaged Drinking Water (Other Than Packaged Natural Mineral Water) - Specification (Third Revision) (Section 4.2 Total Dissolved Solids (TDS), Pages [3, 4])
Normative Force: MANDATORY

Total Dissolved Solids (TDS): Total dissolved solids shall be between 75 mg/L and 500 mg/L.

DOC-023-v001::4.3::REQ-001.title: Turbidity
DOC-023-v001::4.3::REQ-001.text:
Clause 4.3: Turbidity
Standard: IS 14543 : 2024 - Packaged Drinking Water (Other Than Packaged Natural Mineral Water) - Specification (Third Revision) (Section 4.3 Turbidity, Pages [4, 5])
Normative Force: PROHIBITED

Turbidity: Turbidity shall not exceed 2 NTU.

DOC-023-v001::5.1::REQ-001.title: Chemical Contaminants
DOC-023-v001::5.1::REQ-001.text:
Clause 5.1: Chemical Contaminants
Standard: IS 14543 : 2024 - Packaged Drinking Water (Other Than Packaged Natural Mineral Water) - Specification (Third Revision) (Section 5.1 Chemical Contaminants, Pages [5, 6])
Normative Force: INFORMATIVE

Chemical Contaminants: Lead maximum 0.01 mg/L; Arsenic maximum 0.01 mg/L; Fluoride maximum 1.0 mg/L; Nitrate maximum 45 mg/L.

DOC-023-v001::6.1::REQ-001.title: Microbiological Limits
DOC-023-v001::6.1::REQ-001.text:
Clause 6.1: Microbiological Limits
Standard: IS 14543 : 2024 - Packaged Drinking Water (Other Than Packaged Natural Mineral Water) - Specification (Third Revision) (Section 6.1 Microbiological Limits, Pages [6, 7])
Normative Force: MANDATORY

Microbiological Limits: Total Coliform bacteria shall be absent in 250 mL; Escherichia coli (E. coli) shall be absent in 250 mL; Faecal streptococci shall be absent in 250 mL; Pseudomonas aeruginosa shall be absent in 250 mL; Yeast and Mould shall be absent in 250 mL.

DOC-023-v001::7.1::REQ-001.title: Packaging and Labeling
DOC-023-v001::7.1::REQ-001.text:
Clause 7.1: Packaging and Labeling
Standard: IS 14543 : 2024 - Packaged Drinking Water (Other Than Packaged Natural Mineral Water) - Specification (Third Revision) (Section 7.1 Packaging and Labeling, Pages [7, 8])
Normative Force: INFORMATIVE

Packaging and Labeling: Mandatory ISI Mark under Scheme I. Mandatory declaration 'Packaged Drinking Water'.

DOC-024-v001::1::SCOPE-001.title: Scope
DOC-024-v001::1::SCOPE-001.text:
Clause 1: Scope
Standard: IS 13428 : 2005 - Packaged Natural Mineral Water - Specification (Second Revision) (Section 1 Scope, Pages [1])
Normative Force: INFORMATIVE

Scope: This Indian Standard (IS 13428 : 2005) covers and specifies requirements for Packaged Natural Mineral Water - Specification (Second Revision). It applies to packaged_natural_mineral_water under drinking_water category in the food_agriculture domain.

DOC-024-v001::4.1::REQ-001.title: Natural Source
DOC-024-v001::4.1::REQ-001.text:
Clause 4.1: Natural Source
Standard: IS 13428 : 2005 - Packaged Natural Mineral Water - Specification (Second Revision) (Section 4.1 Natural Source, Pages [2, 3])
Normative Force: MANDATORY

Natural Source: Must originate from an underground natural water table or geologically protected spring.

DOC-024-v001::5.1::REQ-001.title: pH Range
DOC-024-v001::5.1::REQ-001.text:
Clause 5.1: pH Range
Standard: IS 13428 : 2005 - Packaged Natural Mineral Water - Specification (Second Revision) (Section 5.1 pH Range, Pages [3, 4])
Normative Force: MANDATORY

pH Range: pH shall be between 6.5 and 8.5.

DOC-024-v001::5.2::REQ-001.title: Total Dissolved Solids
DOC-024-v001::5.2::REQ-001.text:
Clause 5.2: Total Dissolved Solids
Standard: IS 13428 : 2005 - Packaged Natural Mineral Water - Specification (Second Revision) (Section 5.2 Total Dissolved Solids, Pages [4, 5])
Normative Force: INFORMATIVE

Total Dissolved Solids: Between 150 mg/L and 700 mg/L.

DOC-024-v001::6.1::REQ-001.title: Microbiological Criteria
DOC-024-v001::6.1::REQ-001.text:
Clause 6.1: Microbiological Criteria
Standard: IS 13428 : 2005 - Packaged Natural Mineral Water - Specification (Second Revision) (Section 6.1 Microbiological Criteria, Pages [5, 6])
Normative Force: MANDATORY

Microbiological Criteria: E. coli and coliforms shall be absent in 250 mL.

DOC-025-v001::1::SCOPE-001.title: Scope
DOC-025-v001::1::SCOPE-001.text:
Clause 1: Scope
Standard: IS 1165 : 2002 - Milk Powder - Specification (Fifth Revision) (Section 1 Scope, Pages [1])
Normative Force: INFORMATIVE

Scope: This Indian Standard (IS 1165 : 2002) covers and specifies requirements for Milk Powder - Specification (Fifth Revision). It applies to infant_milk_food under dairy_products category in the food_agriculture domain.

DOC-025-v001::4.1::REQ-001.title: Moisture
DOC-025-v001::4.1::REQ-001.text:
Clause 4.1: Moisture
Standard: IS 1165 : 2002 - Milk Powder - Specification (Fifth Revision) (Section 4.1 Moisture, Pages [2, 3])
Normative Force: PROHIBITED

Moisture: Moisture content shall not exceed 4.0% by mass for whole milk powder.

DOC-025-v001::4.2::GEN-001.title: Milk Fat
DOC-025-v001::4.2::GEN-001.text:
Clause 4.2: Milk Fat
Standard: IS 1165 : 2002 - Milk Powder - Specification (Fifth Revision) (Section 4.2 Milk Fat, Pages [3, 4])
Normative Force: PROHIBITED

Milk Fat: Milk fat content shall not be less than 26.0% by mass.

DOC-025-v001::4.3::REQ-001.title: Total Ash
DOC-025-v001::4.3::REQ-001.text:
Clause 4.3: Total Ash
Standard: IS 1165 : 2002 - Milk Powder - Specification (Fifth Revision) (Section 4.3 Total Ash, Pages [4, 5])
Normative Force: PROHIBITED

Total Ash: Total ash on dry basis shall not exceed 7.3%.

DOC-025-v001::4.4::REQ-001.title: Insolubility Index
DOC-025-v001::4.4::REQ-001.text:
Clause 4.4: Insolubility Index
Standard: IS 1165 : 2002 - Milk Powder - Specification (Fifth Revision) (Section 4.4 Insolubility Index, Pages [5, 6])
Normative Force: PROHIBITED

Insolubility Index: Insolubility index shall not exceed 2.0 mL.

DOC-026-v001::1::SCOPE-001.title: Scope
DOC-026-v001::1::SCOPE-001.text:
Clause 1: Scope
Standard: IS 4151 : 2015 - Protective Helmets for Motorcycle Riders - Specification (Fourth Revision) (Section 1 Scope, Pages [1])
Normative Force: INFORMATIVE

Scope: This Indian Standard (IS 4151 : 2015) covers and specifies requirements for Protective Helmets for Motorcycle Riders - Specification (Fourth Revision). It applies to protective_helmets_motorcycle under personal_protective_equipment category in the mechanical_automotive domain.

DOC-026-v001::6.1::REQ-001.title: Helmet Mass
DOC-026-v001::6.1::REQ-001.text:
Clause 6.1: Helmet Mass
Standard: IS 4151 : 2015 - Protective Helmets for Motorcycle Riders - Specification (Fourth Revision) (Section 6.1 Helmet Mass, Pages [2, 3])
Normative Force: PROHIBITED

Helmet Mass: Total mass of complete helmet shall not exceed 1500 g (1.5 kg).

DOC-026-v001::9.1::TEST-001.title: Impact Absorption Test
DOC-026-v001::9.1::TEST-001.text:
Clause 9.1: Impact Absorption Test
Standard: IS 4151 : 2015 - Protective Helmets for Motorcycle Riders - Specification (Fourth Revision) (Section 9.1 Impact Absorption Test, Pages [3, 4])
Normative Force: PROHIBITED

Impact Absorption Test: Headform acceleration shall not exceed 300 g (peak acceleration <= 300 gn) when dropped with impact velocity of 7.5 m/s (kinetic energy ~150 J) onto flat steel anvil and hemispherical anvil.

DOC-026-v001::9.2::REQ-001.title: Retention System Strength
DOC-026-v001::9.2::REQ-001.text:
Clause 9.2: Retention System Strength
Standard: IS 4151 : 2015 - Protective Helmets for Motorcycle Riders - Specification (Fourth Revision) (Section 9.2 Retention System Strength, Pages [4, 5])
Normative Force: PROHIBITED

Retention System Strength: Dynamic extension of chin strap shall not exceed 35 mm under 1 kN dynamic shock load; residual extension shall not exceed 25 mm.

DOC-026-v001::9.3::GEN-001.title: Visor Optical Quality
DOC-026-v001::9.3::GEN-001.text:
Clause 9.3: Visor Optical Quality
Standard: IS 4151 : 2015 - Protective Helmets for Motorcycle Riders - Specification (Fourth Revision) (Section 9.3 Visor Optical Quality, Pages [5, 6])
Normative Force: PROHIBITED

Visor Optical Quality: Luminous transmittance of clear visor shall not be less than 85%.

DOC-026-v001::9.4::REQ-001.title: Visor Mechanical Strength
DOC-026-v001::9.4::REQ-001.text:
Clause 9.4: Visor Mechanical Strength
Standard: IS 4151 : 2015 - Protective Helmets for Motorcycle Riders - Specification (Fourth Revision) (Section 9.4 Visor Mechanical Strength, Pages [6, 7])
Normative Force: INFORMATIVE

Visor Mechanical Strength: High-speed steel ball impact at 60 m/s without visor shattering or puncturing.

DOC-026-v001::10.1::REQ-001.title: Mandatory Marking
DOC-026-v001::10.1::REQ-001.text:
Clause 10.1: Mandatory Marking
Standard: IS 4151 : 2015 - Protective Helmets for Motorcycle Riders - Specification (Fourth Revision) (Section 10.1 Mandatory Marking, Pages [7, 8])
Normative Force: MANDATORY

Mandatory Marking: Mandatory ISI mark, helmet size, month and year of manufacture.

Structured Requirements:
• mandatory_marking_elements: mandatory Trade mark, rated voltage, rated wattage, rated frequency, standard mark None [Status: mandatory]

DOC-027-v001::1::SCOPE-001.title: Scope
DOC-027-v001::1::SCOPE-001.text:
Clause 1: Scope
Standard: IS 2347 : 2017 - Domestic Pressure Cookers - Specification (Fifth Revision) (Section 1 Scope, Pages [1])
Normative Force: INFORMATIVE

Scope: This Indian Standard (IS 2347 : 2017) covers and specifies requirements for Domestic Pressure Cookers - Specification (Fifth Revision). It applies to domestic_pressure_cookers under domestic_appliances_gas category in the mechanical_automotive domain.

DOC-027-v001::7.1::REQ-001.title: Operating Pressure
DOC-027-v001::7.1::REQ-001.text:
Clause 7.1: Operating Pressure
Standard: IS 2347 : 2017 - Domestic Pressure Cookers - Specification (Fifth Revision) (Section 7.1 Operating Pressure, Pages [2, 3])
Normative Force: MANDATORY

Operating Pressure: Operating pressure regulated by weight valve shall be 1.0 bar (100 kPa ± 10 kPa).

DOC-027-v001::7.2::REQ-001.title: Safety Pressure Release Device
DOC-027-v001::7.2::REQ-001.text:
Clause 7.2: Safety Pressure Release Device
Standard: IS 2347 : 2017 - Domestic Pressure Cookers - Specification (Fifth Revision) (Section 7.2 Safety Pressure Release Device, Pages [3, 4])
Normative Force: MANDATORY

Safety Pressure Release Device: Safety valve/fusible plug shall release pressure between 1.4 bar and 2.0 bar (140 kPa to 200 kPa).

DOC-027-v001::8.1::TEST-001.title: Hydraulic Bursting Pressure Test
DOC-027-v001::8.1::TEST-001.text:
Clause 8.1: Hydraulic Bursting Pressure Test
Standard: IS 2347 : 2017 - Domestic Pressure Cookers - Specification (Fifth Revision) (Section 8.1 Hydraulic Bursting Pressure Test, Pages [4, 5])
Normative Force: MANDATORY

Hydraulic Bursting Pressure Test: The cooker body and lid assembly shall withstand hydraulic proof pressure of not less than 3.0 bar (300 kPa) without permanent deformation or leakage.

DOC-027-v001::8.2::TEST-001.title: Thermal Shock Test
DOC-027-v001::8.2::TEST-001.text:
Clause 8.2: Thermal Shock Test
Standard: IS 2347 : 2017 - Domestic Pressure Cookers - Specification (Fifth Revision) (Section 8.2 Thermal Shock Test, Pages [5, 6])
Normative Force: INFORMATIVE

Thermal Shock Test: Heated dry cooker immersed in cold water without warping or cracking.

DOC-028-v001::1::SCOPE-001.title: Scope
DOC-028-v001::1::SCOPE-001.text:
Clause 1: Scope
Standard: IS 15298 (Part 2) : 2016 - Personal Protective Equipment - Safety Footwear (Second Revision) (Section 1 Scope, Pages [1])
Normative Force: INFORMATIVE

Scope: This Indian Standard (IS 15298 (Part 2) : 2016) covers and specifies requirements for Personal Protective Equipment - Safety Footwear (Second Revision). It applies to safety_footwear under personal_protective_equipment category in the mechanical_automotive domain.

DOC-028-v001::5.3.2.2::GEN-001.title: Impact Resistance
DOC-028-v001::5.3.2.2::GEN-001.text:
Clause 5.3.2.2: Impact Resistance
Standard: IS 15298 (Part 2) : 2016 - Personal Protective Equipment - Safety Footwear (Second Revision) (Section 5.3.2.2 Impact Resistance, Pages [2, 3])
Normative Force: MANDATORY

Impact Resistance: Steel toecap shall withstand impact energy of 200 J with minimum clearance under toecap >= 14.0 mm for size 8.

DOC-028-v001::5.3.2.3::GEN-001.title: Compression Resistance
DOC-028-v001::5.3.2.3::GEN-001.text:
Clause 5.3.2.3: Compression Resistance
Standard: IS 15298 (Part 2) : 2016 - Personal Protective Equipment - Safety Footwear (Second Revision) (Section 5.3.2.3 Compression Resistance, Pages [3, 4])
Normative Force: MANDATORY

Compression Resistance: Toecap shall withstand compression load of 15 kN with minimum clearance >= 14.0 mm.

DOC-028-v001::5.8.1::REQ-001.title: Slip Resistance
DOC-028-v001::5.8.1::REQ-001.text:
Clause 5.8.1: Slip Resistance
Standard: IS 15298 (Part 2) : 2016 - Personal Protective Equipment - Safety Footwear (Second Revision) (Section 5.8.1 Slip Resistance, Pages [4, 5])
Normative Force: MANDATORY

Slip Resistance: Dynamic friction coefficient on ceramic tile with NaLS lubricant shall be >= 0.32 for forward heel slip.

DOC-029-v001::1::SCOPE-001.title: Scope
DOC-029-v001::1::SCOPE-001.text:
Clause 1: Scope
Standard: IS 16046 (Part 2) : 2018 - Secondary Cells and Batteries Containing Alkaline or Other Non-Acid Electrolytes - Secondary Lithium Cells and Batteries - Part 2: Portable Applications (Section 1 Scope, Pages [1])
Normative Force: INFORMATIVE

Scope: This Indian Standard (IS 16046 (Part 2) : 2018) covers and specifies requirements for Secondary Cells and Batteries Containing Alkaline or Other Non-Acid Electrolytes - Secondary Lithium Cells and Batteries - Part 2: Portable Applications. It applies to lithium_ion_cells_batteries under secondary_cells category in the batteries_storage domain.

DOC-029-v001::7.2.1::REQ-001.title: Continuous Charging
DOC-029-v001::7.2.1::REQ-001.text:
Clause 7.2.1: Continuous Charging
Standard: IS 16046 (Part 2) : 2018 - Secondary Cells and Batteries Containing Alkaline or Other Non-Acid Electrolytes - Secondary Lithium Cells and Batteries - Part 2: Portable Applications (Section 7.2.1 Continuous Charging, Pages [2, 3])
Normative Force: INFORMATIVE

Continuous Charging: Fully charged cells subjected to continuous 28-day charging without fire or explosion.

DOC-029-v001::7.3.2::REQ-001.title: External Short Circuit
DOC-029-v001::7.3.2::REQ-001.text:
Clause 7.3.2: External Short Circuit
Standard: IS 16046 (Part 2) : 2018 - Secondary Cells and Batteries Containing Alkaline or Other Non-Acid Electrolytes - Secondary Lithium Cells and Batteries - Part 2: Portable Applications (Section 7.3.2 External Short Circuit, Pages [3, 4])
Normative Force: PROHIBITED

External Short Circuit: Short circuit at 55°C with external resistance < 80 mΩ; cell shall not catch fire or explode; case temperature shall not exceed 150°C.

DOC-029-v001::7.3.3::TEST-001.title: Free Fall Test
DOC-029-v001::7.3.3::TEST-001.text:
Clause 7.3.3: Free Fall Test
Standard: IS 16046 (Part 2) : 2018 - Secondary Cells and Batteries Containing Alkaline or Other Non-Acid Electrolytes - Secondary Lithium Cells and Batteries - Part 2: Portable Applications (Section 7.3.3 Free Fall Test, Pages [4, 5])
Normative Force: INFORMATIVE

Free Fall Test: Dropped from 1.0 m height onto concrete floor twice per side without leakage or rupture.

DOC-029-v001::7.3.4::TEST-001.title: Thermal Abuse Test
DOC-029-v001::7.3.4::TEST-001.text:
Clause 7.3.4: Thermal Abuse Test
Standard: IS 16046 (Part 2) : 2018 - Secondary Cells and Batteries Containing Alkaline or Other Non-Acid Electrolytes - Secondary Lithium Cells and Batteries - Part 2: Portable Applications (Section 7.3.4 Thermal Abuse Test, Pages [5, 6])
Normative Force: INFORMATIVE

Thermal Abuse Test: Heated in gravity convection oven to 130°C and held for 10 min without fire or explosion.

DOC-029-v001::7.3.6::TEST-001.title: Crush Test
DOC-029-v001::7.3.6::TEST-001.text:
Clause 7.3.6: Crush Test
Standard: IS 16046 (Part 2) : 2018 - Secondary Cells and Batteries Containing Alkaline or Other Non-Acid Electrolytes - Secondary Lithium Cells and Batteries - Part 2: Portable Applications (Section 7.3.6 Crush Test, Pages [6, 7])
Normative Force: INFORMATIVE

Crush Test: Crushed between hydraulic plates with 13 kN force without explosion.

DOC-029-v001::7.3.8::TEST-001.title: Overcharge Test
DOC-029-v001::7.3.8::TEST-001.text:
Clause 7.3.8: Overcharge Test
Standard: IS 16046 (Part 2) : 2018 - Secondary Cells and Batteries Containing Alkaline or Other Non-Acid Electrolytes - Secondary Lithium Cells and Batteries - Part 2: Portable Applications (Section 7.3.8 Overcharge Test, Pages [7, 8])
Normative Force: INFORMATIVE

Overcharge Test: Overcharged with 2x rated current to 1.2x maximum voltage without explosion.

DOC-030-v001::1::SCOPE-001.title: Scope
DOC-030-v001::1::SCOPE-001.text:
Clause 1: Scope
Standard: IS 616 : 2017 - Audio, Video and Similar Electronic Apparatus - Safety Requirements (Fourth Revision) (Section 1 Scope, Pages [1])
Normative Force: INFORMATIVE

Scope: This Indian Standard (IS 616 : 2017) covers and specifies requirements for Audio, Video and Similar Electronic Apparatus - Safety Requirements (Fourth Revision). It applies to televisions under audio_video category in the electronics_it domain.

DOC-030-v001::9.1::REQ-001.title: Electric Shock Hazard
DOC-030-v001::9.1::REQ-001.text:
Clause 9.1: Electric Shock Hazard
Standard: IS 616 : 2017 - Audio, Video and Similar Electronic Apparatus - Safety Requirements (Fourth Revision) (Section 9.1 Electric Shock Hazard, Pages [2, 3])
Normative Force: PROHIBITED

Electric Shock Hazard: Open circuit voltage of accessible parts shall not exceed 35 V peak AC or 60 V DC under normal operation.

DOC-030-v001::10.3::REQ-001.title: Insulation Resistance
DOC-030-v001::10.3::REQ-001.text:
Clause 10.3: Insulation Resistance
Standard: IS 616 : 2017 - Audio, Video and Similar Electronic Apparatus - Safety Requirements (Fourth Revision) (Section 10.3 Insulation Resistance, Pages [3, 4])
Normative Force: MANDATORY

Insulation Resistance: Shall not be less than 4 MΩ between mains plug and accessible enclosure.

Structured Requirements:
• insulation_resistance: >= 4.0 MΩ [Status: mandatory]

DOC-030-v001::14.1::REQ-001.title: Flame Retardance
DOC-030-v001::14.1::REQ-001.text:
Clause 14.1: Flame Retardance
Standard: IS 616 : 2017 - Audio, Video and Similar Electronic Apparatus - Safety Requirements (Fourth Revision) (Section 14.1 Flame Retardance, Pages [4, 5])
Normative Force: MANDATORY

Flame Retardance: Printed board flammability shall conform to Class V-0 or V-1.

DOC-030-v001::18.1::REQ-001.title: Mechanical Strength
DOC-030-v001::18.1::REQ-001.text:
Clause 18.1: Mechanical Strength
Standard: IS 616 : 2017 - Audio, Video and Similar Electronic Apparatus - Safety Requirements (Fourth Revision) (Section 18.1 Mechanical Strength, Pages [5, 6])
Normative Force: INFORMATIVE

Mechanical Strength: 0.5 J impact hammer test on television display screen without glass implosion or injury.

DOC-031-v001::1::SCOPE-001.title: Scope
DOC-031-v001::1::SCOPE-001.text:
Clause 1: Scope
Standard: IS 13252 (Part 1) : 2010 - Information Technology Equipment - Safety - Part 1: General Requirements (Second Revision) (Section 1 Scope, Pages [1])
Normative Force: INFORMATIVE

Scope: This Indian Standard (IS 13252 (Part 1) : 2010) covers and specifies requirements for Information Technology Equipment - Safety - Part 1: General Requirements (Second Revision). It applies to laptops_notebooks under it_equipment category in the electronics_it domain.

DOC-031-v001::2.1::REQ-001.title: Protection from Electric Shock
DOC-031-v001::2.1::REQ-001.text:
Clause 2.1: Protection from Electric Shock
Standard: IS 13252 (Part 1) : 2010 - Information Technology Equipment - Safety - Part 1: General Requirements (Second Revision) (Section 2.1 Protection from Electric Shock, Pages [2, 3])
Normative Force: PROHIBITED

Protection from Electric Shock: SELV (Safety Extra Low Voltage) circuit shall not exceed 42.4 V peak AC or 60 V DC.

DOC-031-v001::5.1::REQ-001.title: Touch Current
DOC-031-v001::5.1::REQ-001.text:
Clause 5.1: Touch Current
Standard: IS 13252 (Part 1) : 2010 - Information Technology Equipment - Safety - Part 1: General Requirements (Second Revision) (Section 5.1 Touch Current, Pages [3, 4])
Normative Force: PROHIBITED

Touch Current: Maximum touch current for Class I IT equipment shall not exceed 3.5 mA.

DOC-031-v001::5.2::REQ-001.title: Electric Strength
DOC-031-v001::5.2::REQ-001.text:
Clause 5.2: Electric Strength
Standard: IS 13252 (Part 1) : 2010 - Information Technology Equipment - Safety - Part 1: General Requirements (Second Revision) (Section 5.2 Electric Strength, Pages [4, 5])
Normative Force: MANDATORY

Electric Strength: Primary to SELV isolation shall withstand 3000 V AC (or 4242 V DC) for 1 min.

Structured Requirements:
• dielectric_electric_strength: == 4000 V a.c. [Status: mandatory]

DOC-031-v001::4.2::TEST-001.title: Stability Test
DOC-031-v001::4.2::TEST-001.text:
Clause 4.2: Stability Test
Standard: IS 13252 (Part 1) : 2010 - Information Technology Equipment - Safety - Part 1: General Requirements (Second Revision) (Section 4.2 Stability Test, Pages [5, 6])
Normative Force: PROHIBITED

Stability Test: Laptop power adapter shall not tilt over on 10° inclined plane.

DOC-032-v001::1::SCOPE-001.title: Scope
DOC-032-v001::1::SCOPE-001.text:
Clause 1: Scope
Standard: IS 4985 : 2021 - Unplasticized Polyvinyl Chloride (uPVC) Pipes for Potable Water Supplies - Specification (Fourth Revision) (Section 1 Scope, Pages [1])
Normative Force: INFORMATIVE

Scope: This Indian Standard (IS 4985 : 2021) covers and specifies requirements for Unplasticized Polyvinyl Chloride (uPVC) Pipes for Potable Water Supplies - Specification (Fourth Revision). It applies to upvc_pipes_potable_water under polymers_pipes category in the chemicals_polymers domain.

DOC-032-v001::8.1::TEST-001.title: Hydrostatic Pressure Test
DOC-032-v001::8.1::TEST-001.text:
Clause 8.1: Hydrostatic Pressure Test
Standard: IS 4985 : 2021 - Unplasticized Polyvinyl Chloride (uPVC) Pipes for Potable Water Supplies - Specification (Fourth Revision) (Section 8.1 Hydrostatic Pressure Test, Pages [2, 3])
Normative Force: MANDATORY

Hydrostatic Pressure Test: Pipes shall withstand internal hydrostatic pressure test at 27°C with circumferential hoop stress of 10.0 MPa for 1 h without burst.

DOC-032-v001::8.2::TEST-001.title: Long-Term Hydrostatic Test
DOC-032-v001::8.2::TEST-001.text:
Clause 8.2: Long-Term Hydrostatic Test
Standard: IS 4985 : 2021 - Unplasticized Polyvinyl Chloride (uPVC) Pipes for Potable Water Supplies - Specification (Fourth Revision) (Section 8.2 Long-Term Hydrostatic Test, Pages [3, 4])
Normative Force: INFORMATIVE

Long-Term Hydrostatic Test: 1000 h hydrostatic test at 60°C with 4.2 MPa hoop stress without failure.

DOC-032-v001::9.1::TEST-001.title: Impact Test (Falling Weight)
DOC-032-v001::9.1::TEST-001.text:
Clause 9.1: Impact Test (Falling Weight)
Standard: IS 4985 : 2021 - Unplasticized Polyvinyl Chloride (uPVC) Pipes for Potable Water Supplies - Specification (Fourth Revision) (Section 9.1 Impact Test (Falling Weight), Pages [4, 5])
Normative Force: PROHIBITED

Impact Test (Falling Weight): Striker dropped from 2.0 m height on pipe cooled to 0°C; True Impact Rate of Failure (TIR) shall not exceed 10%.

DOC-032-v001::10.1::REQ-001.title: Opacity
DOC-032-v001::10.1::REQ-001.text:
Clause 10.1: Opacity
Standard: IS 4985 : 2021 - Unplasticized Polyvinyl Chloride (uPVC) Pipes for Potable Water Supplies - Specification (Fourth Revision) (Section 10.1 Opacity, Pages [5, 6])
Normative Force: PROHIBITED

Opacity: Light transmission percentage through pipe wall shall not exceed 0.2%.

DOC-033-v001::1::SCOPE-001.title: Scope
DOC-033-v001::1::SCOPE-001.text:
Clause 1: Scope
Standard: IS 15477 : 2019 - Adhesives for Use with Ceramic, Mosaic and Stone Tiles - Specification (First Revision) (Section 1 Scope, Pages [1])
Normative Force: INFORMATIVE

Scope: This Indian Standard (IS 15477 : 2019) covers and specifies requirements for Adhesives for Use with Ceramic, Mosaic and Stone Tiles - Specification (First Revision). It applies to cement_paints under paints_coatings category in the chemicals_polymers domain.

DOC-033-v001::5.1::REQ-001.title: Tensile Adhesion Strength
DOC-033-v001::5.1::REQ-001.text:
Clause 5.1: Tensile Adhesion Strength
Standard: IS 15477 : 2019 - Adhesives for Use with Ceramic, Mosaic and Stone Tiles - Specification (First Revision) (Section 5.1 Tensile Adhesion Strength, Pages [2, 3])
Normative Force: MANDATORY

Tensile Adhesion Strength: Type 2 tile adhesive 28-day tensile adhesion strength shall be >= 1.0 N/mm² under dry conditions.

DOC-033-v001::5.2::REQ-001.title: Shear Adhesion Strength
DOC-033-v001::5.2::REQ-001.text:
Clause 5.2: Shear Adhesion Strength
Standard: IS 15477 : 2019 - Adhesives for Use with Ceramic, Mosaic and Stone Tiles - Specification (First Revision) (Section 5.2 Shear Adhesion Strength, Pages [3, 4])
Normative Force: MANDATORY

Shear Adhesion Strength: Shear adhesion strength after 14 days dry curing shall be >= 1.25 N/mm².

DOC-033-v001::5.3::REQ-001.title: Open Time
DOC-033-v001::5.3::REQ-001.text:
Clause 5.3: Open Time
Standard: IS 15477 : 2019 - Adhesives for Use with Ceramic, Mosaic and Stone Tiles - Specification (First Revision) (Section 5.3 Open Time, Pages [4, 5])
Normative Force: MANDATORY

Open Time: Tensile adhesion strength after 20 min open time shall be >= 0.5 N/mm².

DOC-034-v001::1::SCOPE-001.title: Scope
DOC-034-v001::1::SCOPE-001.text:
Clause 1: Scope
Standard: IS 1786 : 2024 - High Strength Deformed Steel Bars and Wires for Concrete Reinforcement - Specification (Fifth Revision) (Section 1 Scope, Pages [1])
Normative Force: INFORMATIVE

Scope: This Indian Standard (IS 1786 : 2024) covers and specifies requirements for High Strength Deformed Steel Bars and Wires for Concrete Reinforcement - Specification (Fifth Revision). It applies to high_strength_deformed_steel_bars under steel_metals category in the construction_civil domain.

DOC-034-v001::7.1::REQ-001.title: Yield Stress
DOC-034-v001::7.1::REQ-001.text:
Clause 7.1: Yield Stress
Standard: IS 1786 : 2024 - High Strength Deformed Steel Bars and Wires for Concrete Reinforcement - Specification (Fifth Revision) (Section 7.1 Yield Stress, Pages [2, 3])
Normative Force: INFORMATIVE

Yield Stress: Fe 500D minimum proof stress 500 MPa; Fe 550D minimum 550 MPa; Fe 650 minimum 650 MPa (new high-grade steel introduction).

DOC-034-v001::7.2::REQ-001.title: Tensile Strength
DOC-034-v001::7.2::REQ-001.text:
Clause 7.2: Tensile Strength
Standard: IS 1786 : 2024 - High Strength Deformed Steel Bars and Wires for Concrete Reinforcement - Specification (Fifth Revision) (Section 7.2 Tensile Strength, Pages [3, 4])
Normative Force: INFORMATIVE

Tensile Strength: For Fe 500D, minimum tensile strength 565 MPa (TS/YS ratio >= 1.12 for seismic earthquake resistance zones).

DOC-034-v001::7.3::REQ-001.title: Elongation
DOC-034-v001::7.3::REQ-001.text:
Clause 7.3: Elongation
Standard: IS 1786 : 2024 - High Strength Deformed Steel Bars and Wires for Concrete Reinforcement - Specification (Fifth Revision) (Section 7.3 Elongation, Pages [4, 5])
Normative Force: INFORMATIVE

Elongation: Fe 500D minimum elongation increased to 16.0% (enhanced ductility).

DOC-034-v001::4.1::REQ-001.title: Chemical Composition
DOC-034-v001::4.1::REQ-001.text:
Clause 4.1: Chemical Composition
Standard: IS 1786 : 2024 - High Strength Deformed Steel Bars and Wires for Concrete Reinforcement - Specification (Fifth Revision) (Section 4.1 Chemical Composition, Pages [5, 6])
Normative Force: INFORMATIVE

Chemical Composition: Maximum Carbon 0.25%, Sulphur 0.040%, Phosphorus 0.040% for Fe 500D (stricter purity limit).

DOC-035-v001::1::SCOPE-001.title: Scope

Standard: IS 374 : 2026 - Electric Ceiling Fans - Specification (Fifth Revision - Energy Star Mandatory) (Section 1 Scope, Pages [1])
Normative Force: INFORMATIVE

DOC-035-v001::8.1::REQ-001.title: Air Delivery
DOC-035-v001::8.1::REQ-001.text:
Clause 8.1: Air Delivery
Standard: IS 374 : 2026 - Electric Ceiling Fans - Specification (Fifth Revision - Energy Star Mandatory) (Section 8.1 Air Delivery, Pages [2, 3])
Normative Force: MANDATORY

Air Delivery: The minimum air delivery for 1200 mm sweep BLDC ceiling fans shall be 220 m³/min at rated voltage (increased from 210 m³/min).

DOC-035-v001::8.2::REQ-001.title: Power Input
DOC-035-v001::8.2::REQ-001.text:
Clause 8.2: Power Input
Standard: IS 374 : 2026 - Electric Ceiling Fans - Specification (Fifth Revision - Energy Star Mandatory) (Section 8.2 Power Input, Pages [3, 4])
Normative Force: PROHIBITED

Power Input: Maximum power input for 1200 mm fans shall not exceed 35 W for BLDC motors (reduced from 50 W).

DOC-035-v001::8.3::REQ-001.title: Service Value
DOC-035-v001::8.3::REQ-001.text:
Clause 8.3: Service Value
Standard: IS 374 : 2026 - Electric Ceiling Fans - Specification (Fifth Revision - Energy Star Mandatory) (Section 8.3 Service Value, Pages [4, 5])
Normative Force: INFORMATIVE

Service Value: Minimum service value increased to 6.28 m³/min/W for Star 1 rating.

DOC-035-v001::9.1::REQ-001.title: Temperature Rise
DOC-035-v001::9.1::REQ-001.text:
Clause 9.1: Temperature Rise
Standard: IS 374 : 2026 - Electric Ceiling Fans - Specification (Fifth Revision - Energy Star Mandatory) (Section 9.1 Temperature Rise, Pages [5, 6])
